sections.h2: Maize ethanol falls Rs 3 a litre but stays the dearest feedstock

chart.title: Maize, at Rs 68.86, stays Rs 4.86 a litre above damaged grain
chart.sub: Price paid per litre of ethanol, Rs, by feedstock, ESY 2026-27 tender (basic rate plus incentive).

sections.means: The basic rates are unchanged, so the only price cut is the maize incentive, and maize still costs the most of any feedstock still bought.
sections.todo: Distillers should press for the maize incentive cut to be reviewed, as the All India Distillers' Association has asked, before the bids close on 29 October.

sections.h2: Cane juice, sugar and B-heavy supply, 26.4% last year, is not sought

chart.title: Cane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses, 26% of last year's supply, are not sought
chart.sub: Share of last year's allocation (about 1,048 crore litres), % by feedstock.
chart.source: ChiniMandi data via BioEnergy Times; tender 26985.

sections.means: Cane-based ethanol supplied about a quarter of last year's allocation, and this tender removes it entirely, leaving grain to carry the programme.
sections.todo: Watch the offers from distilleries built on cane juice and B-heavy molasses, since the post says it cannot see whether those plants will keep running.

sections.h2: Allocation flips from sugar-first to cheapest-first, putting maize last

chart.title: Maize moves from equal footing with grain to last in line
events: Zones short of supply take all offers; surplus zones fill sugar, syrup and cane juice before molasses and grain
No zones; cooperative sugar mills and long-term-contract plants come first, then the cheapest feedstock first
Maize comes last, after C-heavy molasses, other feedstocks, FCI rice and damaged grain

sections.means: Because maize is the dearest feedstock, it is allocated only after cheaper offers run out, unless the plant has a long-term contract or is a cooperative.
